sources.author: G. Cliff
sources.examined: SIZE OF PREY, journal p113 / PDF p10
sources.finding: Same-species stomach-content evidence includes intact swallowed prey and prey reduced to pieces; repeated processing is not obligatory. Predator lengths in this paper are precaudal lengths, not total lengths.
sources.limit: Stomach contents do not reveal measured motion frequency, sequence or exact3D joint angles. Copyrighted reference, not a production texture.

sources.author: Motta, Tricas, Hueter and Summers
sources.finding: Large food can be gripped between jaws then processed through vigorous lateral head and body movement; upper teeth cut while the prey is held.
sources.limit: Related carcharhinid mechanism, not measured Sphyrna mokarran kinematics; not a rule that every shark shakes every prey. Copyrighted reference.

sources.examined: Abstract only; full text unavailable in prior research
sources.finding: Grasp-turning is a burst/tight turning prey-capture behavior. It must not be equated with all lateral prey processing or all feeding.
sources.limit: No original continuous video inspected from this paper; no angle/frequency calibration.

decision: Use separate small-prey ingestion and large-food processing branches. Size relative to mouth, food shape and resistance matter; do not use a universal length threshold. R4 lateral reversals are authored qualitative demonstrations, not copied or calibrated animation.
asset_reuse: References support independent factual/motion research; no third-party geometry, animation or footage included in game production assets. Local reference permission is not a blanket commercial license.
